mechanism: Anticipate that future self will face temptation or weakness. Remove future options by present action. Examples: delete the app, announce publicly, create penalty for deviation. Cost of breaking commitment must exceed temptation value. It constructs an {{oath_bind}} contract that penalizes future deviation from the chosen path.
failure_modes: Over-commitment: Binding too early locks out legitimate pivots when new information arrives.

Silent lapse: the penalty was sufficient at binding time and is no longer — temptation grew, the penalty's value decayed, or the enforcing party stopped enforcing. Nothing in the device detects this, so a lapsed commitment continues to read as binding.
invariants: The cost of deviation is stated in advance and enforceable by a party other than the committer.
Irrevocability: {{agent}} cannot unilaterally remove the constraint.

_meta.caution: Removes future options by design — can trap agent in suboptimal commitment.
